title: SEBI debt categories by borrower, plus target maturity funds
objectives: Explain gilt, banking & PSU, corporate bond, credit risk and floater categories by their minimum allocations.
Say what a target maturity fund promises — and what it does not.
body_md:
Gilt funds hold at least 80% in government securities: no credit risk, but possibly high rate risk. Gilt with 10-year constant duration holds at least 80% in G-secs at about 10 years' Macaulay duration: pure long-rate exposure. Banking & PSU funds hold at least 80% in debt of banks, PSUs and public financial institutions. Corporate bond funds hold at least 80% in AA+ and above corporate bonds. Credit risk funds hold at least 65% in bonds rated AA and below: higher yield for higher default risk. Floater funds hold at least 65% in floating-rate instruments: lower rate risk. Target maturity funds/ETFs are passive funds holding bonds maturing around one date; held to maturity, the return is close to the YTM at purchase, after costs, though not guaranteed. Hybrid funds (conservative hybrid, arbitrage, equity savings) are not pure debt funds; explain the equity part separately.

| Category | What SEBI requires | Key point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gilt | At least 80% in government securities | No credit risk; can have high rate risk |
| Gilt with 10-year constant duration | At least 80% in G-secs, portfolio Macaulay duration about 10 years | Pure long-rate exposure |
| Banking & PSU | At least 80% in debt of banks, PSUs, public financial institutions | Generally high quality |
| Corporate bond | At least 80% in AA+ and above rated corporate bonds | Higher-quality corporate credit |
| Credit risk | At least 65% in bonds rated AA and below | Higher yield for higher default risk |
| Floater | At least 65% in floating-rate instruments | Lower rate risk |

> **Investor takeaway:** Don't choose a debt fund by last year's return. Choose by duration first, credit quality second, cost third.
example: Bharat Bond ETFs are target maturity funds: held to maturity, the return is close to the starting YTM after costs, though not guaranteed.
say: Gilt means no credit risk, but rate risk remains.
A credit risk fund's higher yield is payment for higher default risk.
never: Credit risk funds are the safest debt funds.
Target maturity returns are guaranteed if held to maturity.
